strengths: Strong motivation and problem formulation: RTL quality estimation directly from pre-synthesis representations is an impactful problem in EDA. The paper clearly articulates the shortcomings of token-based LLM approaches (lack of explicit structural semantics) and hand-crafted graph features.

Well-tailored pretraining design: Masking post-GNN context-aware embeddings rather than raw node features/edges is a principled solution to avoid syntactic and functional ambiguity inherent in CDFGs. Combining stratified masking with class-balanced focal loss effectively addresses the severe node class imbalance.

Effective cross-stage knowledge distillation: Transferring representations from a post-mapping netlist GNN teacher to the RTL CDFG student model bridges the abstraction gap between RTL code and physical realization in a well-grounded manner.

Substantial empirical gains on a sizable dataset: Experiments on 13,200 designs demonstrate noticeable improvements in R² and error metrics over strong Verilog LLMs (CodeV variants) and standard graph baselines, both with and without distillation.
weaknesses: Scalability and computational complexity on large CDFGs: Table 3 reveals that CDFGs can contain up to 19,169 nodes (with hundreds of designs exceeding 5,000–10,000 nodes). The paper employs an 8-layer full Transformer encoder. Because standard multi-head self-attention scales quadratically with node count O(|V|²), the paper does not clarify how the Transformer handles sequences of over 10k nodes without running out of memory, nor does it report inference/training latency or memory benchmarks.

Lack of direct Graph SSL baselines: The central methodological justification is that direct masking (e.g., GraphMAE, MaskGAE) fails on computational graphs due to functional ambiguity. However, the evaluation lacks empirical comparisons against standard GraphMAE and MaskGAE applied directly to CDFGs, leaving this specific claim supported primarily by intuition rather than comparative empirical data.

Evaluation setup and risk of data leakage: The 13,200 designs sourced from VeriGen and DeepCircuitX are split randomly (80:20). Hardware designs in public corpora often contain repeated synthetic variants, parameterized module instantiations, or overlapping submodules. A module-level or benchmark-level out-of-distribution split (testing on genuinely unseen hardware designs) would provide a much more rigorous evaluation of generalizability.

Missing reproducibility details and error bars: In the Appendix under 'Code Implementation', the repository link is left blank ('available in the anonymous GitHub repository: .'). Additionally, experimental results in Tables 1 and 2 report single-point estimates without standard deviations across random seeds.

strengths: The paper addresses a significant challenge in EDA: providing fast and accurate pre-synthesis RTL quality estimation (area and delay) without running slow logic synthesis tools.

The transition from token-based LLM representations to structure-informed Control Data Flow Graphs (CDFGs) is well-motivated, explicitly capturing data and control dependencies that are essential for physical metric estimation.

The pretraining design incorporates thoughtful domain-specific adjustments: applying masking on post-GNN embeddings rather than raw operations avoids functional ambiguity, while stratified masking and class-balanced focal loss effectively tackle the extreme node frequency imbalance (e.g., wires vs. rare arithmetic operators).

Cross-stage knowledge distillation effectively leverages post-mapping (PM) netlist representations during training to guide the RTL-stage CDFG predictor without incurring inference-time synthesis overhead.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation on 13,200 designs demonstrates clear improvements over both graph baselines and LLM-based baselines (CodeV variants) across multiple metrics (MAE, MAPE, R², RRSE), supported by ablation studies.
weaknesses: The dataset evaluation relies solely on a random 80/20 train/validation split. Sourcing designs from VeriGen and DeepCircuitX often results in synthetic variants or shared module families, where random splitting risks data leakage; an out-of-distribution (OOD) or split by repository/circuit type would provide a more rigorous test of generalization.

Scalability of the Transformer encoder is underexplored. Table 3 shows designs reaching up to 19,169 nodes, yet standard full self-attention exhibits quadratic complexity O(N²). The authors do not clarify how graphs with thousands of nodes are batched, truncated, or accommodated within GPU memory alongside the 16-dimensional Laplacian eigenvector projection.
The repository URL is omitted in the Appendix ('available in the anonymous GitHub repository: .'), hindering verification of reproducibility and open-source release.
All reported evaluation metrics lack standard deviations across multiple runs or different random seeds, making it difficult to assess statistical significance.

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing a critical bottleneck in EDA: estimating post-synthesis quality metrics directly from RTL without running expensive synthesis tools.

Convincing empirical demonstration that explicit structural modeling on CDFGs outperforms both token-based LLM baselines (such as 7B-parameter CodeV models) and conventional graph methods across area and delay prediction.
Effective integration of cross-stage knowledge distillation from post-mapping netlist representations to enhance the fidelity of RTL-level predictions.
Well-crafted pretraining adaptations for hardware graphs, including stratified masking and class-balanced focal loss to address the severe skew between storage elements and arithmetic operator nodes.
The paper is clearly structured and well-written, supported by informative diagrams and algorithmic formulations.
weaknesses: Lack of explanation regarding Transformer scalability on large graphs: Table 3 indicates designs contain up to 19,169 nodes (with over 2,500 graphs exceeding 600 nodes). Standard full self-attention scales quadratically ($O(N^2)$), yet the paper does not specify how large graphs are handled (e.g., whether truncation, sparse attention, or sub-graphing is used) or provide memory and inference latency benchmarks.

Evaluation protocol and split strategy: The dataset is split into an 80:20 train/validation split without specifying whether splitting is performed randomly or grouped by repository/source family. Random splitting on circuit benchmarks often results in data contamination and optimistic performance due to syntactically similar design variants.

Incomplete ablations of core technical motivations: The authors argue that masking post-GNN representations is essential to resolve semantic ambiguity inherent in raw CDFG nodes, yet there is no experimental ablation comparing post-GNN masking against standard input-level masking (e.g., GraphMAE style). Furthermore, the contribution of the global Laplacian positional embeddings (LapPE) is not ablated.
Missing code link: The Appendix states that the code and datasets are available at an anonymous repository, but the URL is left blank ('repository: .').

strengths: The paper addresses a critical bottleneck in digital circuit design by predicting post-synthesis quality metrics (area and delay) directly from RTL, achieving a ~145x speedup over conventional synthesis toolchains.

The technical design is well-motivated by domain characteristics: using CDFGs instead of token sequences explicitly exposes structural and dataflow dependencies; masking post-GNN context embeddings avoids functional ambiguity of raw operators; and stratified masking addresses severe class imbalance across hardware primitive types.

StructRTL achieves state-of-the-art results across all metrics, substantially outperforming both graph baselines and 7B-parameter LLM-based approaches (e.g., VeriDistill / CodeV) with a compact 30M parameter model.

The experimental evaluation is exceptionally comprehensive, covering ablations of all architectural and pretraining components, out-of-distribution functional and size generalization splits, few-shot calibration performance, and pairwise ranking on 51 industrial design pairs.
weaknesses: From a pure machine learning methodology perspective, the framework largely synthesizes existing paradigms (GNN-Transformer hybrid architecture with Laplacian positional encodings, masked graph autoencoding, and feature-level knowledge distillation) rather than introducing fundamentally new learning algorithms.

Scalability of the full Transformer encoder to very large designs is constrained by quadratic complexity: peak memory reaches ~52GB at 20,000 CDFG nodes. Although register-boundary partitioning is explored as a mitigation, full-chip industrial RTL can easily exceed hundreds of thousands of nodes.

Cross-stage supervision via knowledge distillation requires running full logic synthesis and technology mapping to obtain post-mapping netlists for the training set, coupling teacher training to a specific standard cell library (SkyWater 130nm) and toolchain.

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing a key limitation of recent LLM-based RTL quality estimation methods, properly arguing that Control Data Flow Graphs (CDFGs) capture structural and timing semantics much more explicitly than token sequences.

Thoughtful pretraining design tailored to computational graphs, notably applying masking at the post-GNN context-embedding level rather than raw node features to prevent functional ambiguity, combined with stratified masking and class-balanced focal loss to handle severe class imbalance.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation on a large dataset of 13,200 designs, demonstrating substantial performance improvements over both GNN and 7B-parameter LLM baselines (e.g., significant gains in R² on both area and delay, with and without knowledge distillation).

Thorough ablation and generalization studies, including functional split generalization, size-extrapolation generalization, combinational vs. sequential circuit breakdowns, and pairwise ranking evaluation on 51 industrial design pairs.

High computational efficiency and practicality: with only 30M parameters, StructRTL achieves superior accuracy compared to 7B LLM backbones while delivering 145× speedup over full logic synthesis (~0.096s per design).
weaknesses: Memory scalability issues with the global Transformer encoder: because dense self-attention scales quadratically, peak memory reaches over 50GB for 20K nodes (Figure 9). While a register-boundary partitioning strategy is piloted in Appendix M, it leads to an accuracy drop in area ranking (from 82.35% to 78.43%), and linear/sparse graph transformer architectures are not explored.

Limited exploration of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for LLM baselines: the comparison relies primarily on frozen LLM embeddings or full fine-tuning (which heavily overfitted as shown in Appendix K). Exploring methods like LoRA could have provided a stronger and fairer LLM baseline comparison.

Evaluation restricted to an open-source EDA flow (Yosys/ABC) and a legacy technology library (SkyWater 130nm). Modern industrial flows rely heavily on commercial tools (e.g., Synopsys DC, Cadence Genus) and advanced finFET nodes where interconnect delay and complex physical synthesis effects dominate timing behavior.

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation: Tackling early RTL quality estimation by moving away from purely token-based LLM representations to Control Data Flow Graphs (CDFGs) is theoretically sound and addresses key limitations of both hand-crafted graph features and language model tokenizers in integrated circuit design.

Well-designed pretraining strategy: Masking post-GNN context-aware embeddings instead of raw node features effectively prevents ambiguity in computational operator graphs, while stratified masking and class-balanced focal loss explicitly alleviate the severe long-tail distribution of circuit operators.

Effective cross-stage knowledge distillation: Transferring structural gate-level representations from a post-mapping netlist predictor into the RTL-level predictor provides meaningful inductive bias that bridges the semantic gap between RTL abstractions and physical implementation.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation: The paper evaluates on a large benchmark of 13,200 designs (substantially larger than traditional academic datasets in this domain) and compares against competitive baselines, including three specialized 7B Verilog LLMs (CodeV variants). StructRTL achieves consistent improvements across area and delay metrics.

Extensive out-of-distribution and ablation studies: The authors provide thorough analyses covering functional splits, size-based generalization (training on small, evaluating on large circuits), combinational vs. sequential splits, LLMs on textualized CDFGs, and validation on 102 real industrial modules via pairwise ranking.

Honest discussion of limitations and clear presentation: The manuscript is well-structured, clearly written, and provides detailed appendices on model architecture, runtime/memory scaling, and failure modes.
weaknesses: Evaluation restricted to a single academic/open-source PDK: Experiments rely exclusively on the SkyWater 130nm library and the open-source Yosys/ABC toolchain. In modern commercial semiconductor flows at advanced FinFET nodes, post-synthesis quality is heavily dominated by interconnect parasitics and physical synthesis optimizations, which may present different challenges not captured in this setup.

Handling of sequential circuits: As observed in Table 4, performance drops on sequential circuits, particularly for delay estimation. While inter-cycle flow is present in CDFGs, standard GNN/Transformer layers do not explicitly model setup/hold timing paths or multi-clock domain constraints.

Quadratic memory complexity of global attention: Flattening large CDFGs into Transformer sequences leads to high peak memory usage (reaching over 50GB on 20,000-node graphs as shown in Figure 9). Although register-boundary partitioning is explored as a mitigation in Appendix M, integrating sparse attention or hierarchical graph pooling directly into the core architecture remains an open challenge.
